title: intake-eval-playbook-checklist-v0.9
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook and checklist for taking a new foundation or community model through Redwood's applied-ML onboarding funnel. It is intentionally pragmatic — contains the minimum evaluation steps to make a safe, cost-aware serving decision and to set up ongoing regression detection. Use it for both hosted and dedicated/private onboarding paths.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: new model intake up to production gating (not fully covering infra provisioning or contract/legal).
- Audience: applied-ML engineers, model owners, solutions engineers, and SREs who will be responsible for rollout and monitoring.

Quick intake checklist (short):
1) Intake form complete (model name, source, license, size, quantization targets, expected peak qps, estimated latency SLO).
2) Initial security & license review flagged (legal review if non-permissive).
3) Baseline prompt set selected: 5 canonical tasks + 3 adversarial probes per task.
4) Data privacy review (PII checks for prompts and example inputs).
5) Compute profile run (1k prompt warmup, throughput and memory traces).
6) Cost estimate snapshot (per-1M tokens at expected config).
7) Success criteria agreed and owner assigned.
8) Regression/alert thresholds configured.

Detailed acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Latency: median per-token generation <= target_median_ms (team to fill), p95 <= target_p95_ms.
- Throughput: sustained QPS for expected inference shape with <= 10% degradation under 2x burst for dedicated pools.
- Quality: for each of the 5 canonical tasks, model must meet or exceed baseline metric thresholds (ROUGE/BLEU/EM/embedding-similarity) OR human eval pass-rate >= 85% on sampled prompts.
- Safety: automated toxic-span checks return < 0.5% high-risk outputs on prompt suite; any high-risk output requires mitigation plan.
- Determinism/variance: sampling behavior consistent with seed expectations (if used) or otherwise documented.
- Cost: projected per-token cost must be within X% of target budget for the product owner (tunable per project).

Owner roles and responsibilities:
- Model Owner: primary contact for model behavior and prompt design (example: Priya N.).
- Eval Lead: builds prompt sets, runs evals, curates human annotations (example: Ethan M.).
- Infra Contact: ensures tooling, GPU quantization profiles, and CI integration (example: Ravi K.).
- Security/Legal: approves license and privacy posture (Sofia A.).
- Product Sponsor: signs off on production gating and rollback policy.

Prompt set design and sampling plan:
- Canonical tasks: Identify 5 core product-aligned tasks (e.g., summarization for notes product, instruction-following, code generation, retrieval-augmented QA, classification).
- For each task: 40 prompts broken into: 20 in-distribution (prod-like), 10 edge-case/long-context, 10 adversarial (malformed, jailbreaky, PII).
- Annotation plan: 200 human labels (binary pass/fail + freeform score) per model for the initial gate; sampling stratified by prompt type.
- Synthetic diversity: augment with paraphrases and truncated contexts to test prefix caching and KV eviction behavior.

Regression detection rules (automated):
- Metric drift: 5% drop in embedding similarity or 7% drop in pass-rate on canonical set triggers P0 ticket.
- Latency regressions: sudden 20% increase in median token latency or 30% p95 increase triggers auto-rollover to fallback model variant.
- Safety regressions: any introduction of high-severity flagged output (as per safety classifier) triggers immediate halt to rollout and paging to SRE+Eval team.
- Cost regressions: 25% higher token cost than projection triggers review of quantization or routing.

Evaluation cadence and automation:
- Initial intake: full battery (metrics + human annotations) completed within 2 weeks of intake form submission.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 48 hours with full metric capture.
- Progressive rollout milestones: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24–72 hr observation windows, gating on no regression.
- Nightly automated eval: run canonical prompt set against the production variant; store results and diff against baseline.
- CI hooks: PRs updating prompt sets or model config must run the eval suite and attach results to PR.

Release gating and rollback plan:
- Gate to go-to-canary: must meet latency and safety pass gates and have annotated quality >= threshold.
- Canary kill-switch: immediate fallback to previous stable model if any P0 regression rule fires.
- Rollback timeline: SRE to rollback within 30 minutes of verified regression; postmortem within 72 hours.

Observability and artifacts to collect during testing:
- Token-level latencies, memory traces, KV-cache hit rates, per-prompt outputs, model logits for top-K analysis, embedding vectors and cosine similarity scores, human label IDs and notes.
- Store artifacts in centralized eval bucket with consistent naming: evals/<model>/<date>/<run_id>.

Example minimal prompt set (sketch):
- Summarization: 12 product-like notes, 6 long-context (5k tokens), 6 adversarial (ambiguous referents).
- Instruction: 12 clear instruction prompts; 6 contradictory-instruction probes; 6 safety-jailbreak probes.
- Code: 20 small functions, 10 obfuscated tasks, 10 docs-to-code conversions.

Open questions / trade-offs to decide per intake:
- Human eval budget: which intakes can skip human labels based on historical parity?
- Quantization tolerance: acceptable loss in quality versus cost savings (model-specific).
- Canary sizing: when to use staged ramp vs. immediate 5% for teams under tight deadlines.

Operational checklist before full prod launch (final gate):
- Monitoring dashboards configured with baseline alerts.
- Rollout policy (canary %) encoded in console and infra.
- Playbook published with contacts and runbook links.
- Legal signed off on license and export controls.
- Backfill training for support/CS on expected behavior and known failures.

Next steps (action items):
- Assign Eval Lead and Model Owner in intake form (Due: 2025-01-15).
- Run compute profile job and upload results to eval bucket (Due: 2025-01-20).
- Assemble human annotation pool and template rubric (Due: 2025-01-22).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep checklist lean for smaller community models; heavy enterprise customers require extended compliance + audit logs.
- Consider adding automated prompt generation (LLM-based) for synthetic edge cases later.

Appendix: quick evaluation matrix (text):
- Quality pass-rate (canonical set): pass >= 85%
- Safety high-risk outputs: < 0.5%
- Median token latency: <= product SLO (fill per-intake)
- Cost per 1M tokens: <= budget threshold (fill per-intake)
